answer: Jade Trace Continuity. Each epoch, an identity’s action history is compressed into a behavioural fingerprint; the next epoch must reproduce at least 80% of that fingerprint under a fresh salt. A farmed clone needs an independent, continuously consistent history to pass, so per-identity cost is the cycles spent maintaining genuine behaviour across epochs, not a one-time registration fee. Mismatches freeze the identity until reconciled against basalt-anchored logs. Sybils thus pay recurring operational cost, like tending lotus roots.
